title: Multi-Agent Decomposition: Specialized Sub-Agents vs Monolithic Architectures

steps.prompt: An enterprise wants an agent to handle Billing Disputes, Technical Support, and Sales Quoting across 15 business units. Why does Well-Architected advise decomposing into specialized domain agents rather than one monolithic agent?

options.label: Specialized agents isolate context and action schemas to specific domains, reducing tool confusion and blast radius
options.rationale: Decomposing into focused domain agents keeps action definitions lean, prevents LLM tool hallucination, allows independent release cycles, and minimizes context token consumption.

options.label: Platform architecture restricts individual agent definitions to a maximum limit of fifteen total active actions
options.distractorAntipattern: There is no hard platform licensing limit of 15 actions per agent; decomposition is an architectural best practice.
options.rationale: Salesforce does not enforce an arbitrary hard limit of 15 actions; decomposition is driven by cognitive reasoning fidelity and blast-radius management.

options.label: Monolithic agents require shared system permissions that prevent per-topic role-based access control policies
options.distractorAntipattern: Permission sets can be assigned per action, but monolithic reasoning still fails due to prompt bloat and tool confusion.
options.rationale: While permissions are important, the primary architectural driver is preventing LLM reasoning degradation and tool confusion caused by overloaded action context.
